newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdansk refinery 1996 net drops 63 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdansk refinery 1996 net drops 63 pct.

text.p: The net profit of the second largest Polish refinery, Rafineria Gdanska SA, tumbled 63 percent to 46 million zlotys in 1996 because of high world prices and caps on domestic prices, its president said.
In February the Gdansk refinery said its net profit dropped by 35 percent last year from 125 million zlotys in 1995.
"The price of crude in zlotys rose 25 percent, while sales prices rose only 15 percent and the refinery had to cover the difference," Wlodzimierz Dyrka told reporters on Thursday.
Dyrka said the refinery processed a record 2.95 million tonnes of crude last year, up from 2.85 million in 1995.
Its gross revenues increasd 14 percent to 3.21 billion zlotys and net revenues rose 6.8 percent to 2.25 billion.
Gdansk expected its net to rebound in 1997 after the domestic fuel price cap was lifted in February and said its modernisation programme was not endangered by the lower profit.
The refinery plans to invest $425 million by 1999 to increase processing capability to 4.5 million tonnes per year.
